linkedin.about: Brené Brown is a research professor at the University of Houston, where she holds the Huffington Foundation Endowed Chair at the Graduate College of Social Work. She also holds the position of Professor of Practice in Management at The University of Texas at Austin McCombs School of Business. Brené is the author of six #1 New York Times bestsellers and the host of two award-winning podcasts. Brené spends most of her time working in organizations around the world, helping develop braver leaders and more courageous cultures. In 2024, she was named Executive Chair of the Center for Daring Leadership at BetterUp. She lives in Houston, Texas, with her husband, Steve. They have two children, Ellen and Charlie, and a weird Bichon Frisé named Lucy.

posts.caption:
@adamgrant and I loved talking with @angelalduckworth about her new book, “Situated.”

Big takeaway:

“To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree:

Culture matters.
Mentors matter.
Teammates matter.
Even the objects in your personal space matter.

How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation.”

I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces as reminders of what’s important. It reminds of why I like to write in a room where my children’s art is hanging. The kids’ art is my favorite art and it’s imperfect and honest. Grit is great, but I also need the environment to say, “Have fun. Just start.”

To watch or listen to the episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

To my Longhorn family: Try not to step in the bullshit left behind by small-minded people.
Stay strong. Like UT vs OSU strong. 🧡🤘🏻🤍

Priya Parker, one of my favorite thinkers and writers, is joining @thecuriosityshop this week and we’re talking about fighting! Not “dukes up” fighting but how real heat and conflict can build connection if we’re willing to learn how to do it well.

What I love about this conversation and Priya’s new book - “The Art of Fighting” - is being called to imagine a world where we unlearn and relearn what it means to gather and to disagree. And, she’s just so honest and fun!

To watch or listen to the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Aaron Sandel @prof.sandel, an anthropologist and primatologist, has spent over a decade studying the Ngogo chimpanzees, witnessing one of the largest known chimp communities split into two factions.

Aaron helps Adam and I understand what chimpanzees can teach us about friendship, conflict, belonging, and human nature. He shares what he learned from watching these chimps show affection, navigate dominance hierarchies, and face the effects of division within their own community.

Aaron also reflects on what it was like to watch chimps he knew by name turn against one another, while exploring the surprising depth of bonds in this community.

If you’re trying to find me this semester, I’ll be the one sneaking into Aaron’s class at UT Austin! I have so many more questions!

To listen or watch the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Grateful for a mother who warned her daughters about the price she paid for trying to conform to nice girl culture in the 1950’s. We didn’t know all of the details of her wounds, but we fully understood the depth of her pain. 

When she died she had framed pictures of Gloria Steinem and Angela Davis over her desk.
 
Quote: Gloria Steinem’s remarks at the National Organization for Women’s March for the Equal Rights Amendment, Washington, D.C., July 9, 1978, as reported in James Lardner and Neil Henry, “Over 40,000 ERA Backers March,” Washington Post, July 10, 1978

📸 Warren K. Leffler

Celebrating Dolly has me thinking about the joy of reading books and how often I squander that pleasure by putting myself under pressure to consume pages. 

We are all craving deep reading, deep thinking, and deep connection — and these all require deep time. 

I went back this morning and re-read the interview we did with @mayasmarty and was drawn to her phrase the “privilege of focus.” 

Let’s start a spiritual book club where we read what we want, when we want, no meetings or deadlines - just a shared reframe of deep time as subversive in a world of shallow distraction, addictive scrolling, and unrelenting attention grabbing. ❤️📖❤️

Sometimes shiny is great. Sometimes it’s dangerous.

Episode available on YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

You left our hearts better than you found them. Thank you, Dolly.

David Gahr 📸

analysis.name: Brené Brown
analysis.oneLiner: A research professor and author dedicated to understanding and fostering courage, vulnerability, and wholehearted living, with a deep love for Texas culture and intellectual curiosity.
analysis.summary: Brené Brown is a highly accomplished research professor, #1 New York Times bestselling author, and podcast host, known for her work on courage, vulnerability, shame, and empathy. She holds endowed chairs at the University of Houston and The University of Texas at Austin, and founded the Brené Brown Education and Research Group. Her professional life is dedicated to helping leaders and organizations build braver, more courageous cultures. Outside of her academic and professional pursuits, she is a proud Texan, a devoted mother, and someone who appreciates deep conversations and the joy of reading.

career.ambition: To continue developing and disseminating research on courage, vulnerability, and leadership, impacting organizations globally and fostering deeper human connection through her work and platforms.

needs.label: Intellectual partnership
needs.detail: Her work and social media activity consistently highlight deep dives into complex topics, conversations with academics and authors, and a love for 'deep thinking' and 'deep connection.'

needs.label: Emotional depth and courage
needs.detail: Her entire body of work revolves around vulnerability, courage, shame, and empathy. She discusses 'clear and kind cultures' and 'learning how to fight well' in relationships.

needs.label: Respect for her professional commitments
needs.detail: She holds multiple prestigious academic positions, runs a research group, authors bestsellers, and hosts podcasts, indicating a very demanding and impactful career.

needs.label: A partner who values authenticity
needs.detail: She recounts her mother's 'price she paid for trying to conform to nice girl culture' and praises 'imperfect and honest' art, suggesting a strong aversion to pretense.

needs.label: Shared sense of belonging and community
needs.detail: Her posts about 'Longhorn family,' 'Hook 'em,' and discussions on belonging with primatologists suggest a strong appreciation for community and shared identity.

hobbies.label: Reading and deep thinking
hobbies.detail: She talks about the 'joy of reading books,' 'deep reading, deep thinking, and deep connection,' and consistently engages with other authors' new works.

hobbies.label: Hosting conversations/podcasting
hobbies.detail: She hosts two award-winning podcasts and frequently promotes episodes from 'The Curiosity Shop,' indicating this is a significant activity for her.

hobbies.label: Attending/following sports (specifically Texas Longhorns football)
hobbies.detail: Multiple Instagram posts explicitly mention 'GAME DAY! Hook 'em! 🧡🤍🏈🤍🧡' and 'Like UT vs OSU strong.'

hobbies.label: Writing
hobbies.detail: She is the author of six #1 New York Times bestsellers and frequently shares articles she has written.

interests.label: Human behavior and social dynamics
interests.detail: Her research focuses on courage, vulnerability, shame, empathy, trust, and leadership. She discusses topics like 'conflict avoidant' cultures and what chimps teach us about 'friendship, conflict, belonging, and human nature.'

interests.label: Leadership development and organizational culture
interests.detail: She 'spends most of her time working in organizations around the world, helping develop braver leaders and more courageous cultures.'

interests.label: Philosophy and paradoxes
interests.detail: Article titles like 'Strong Ground and the Tenacity of Paradox,' 'The Courage to Not Know,' and a post about 'The paradox of a pair of clocks' and 'Chronos and Kairos' indicate a fascination with complex concepts.

interests.label: Literature and non-fiction authors
interests.detail: She frequently references and discusses books and authors like Angela Duckworth, Priya Parker, Maya Smarty, and John Green.

interests.label: Texas culture and identity
interests.detail: Her Instagram bio explicitly states 'Texan. HOU + ATX via SATX' and she shows strong affiliation with the Longhorns.

values.label: Courage and Vulnerability
values.detail: This is the core of her professional work and frequently appears in her article titles ('BRAVING TRUST,' 'The Courage to Not Know'). She advocates for 'clear and kind cultures' where 'courage lives.'

values.label: Authenticity and Honesty
values.detail: She values 'imperfect and honest' art and criticizes 'nice' cultures that are actually 'conflict avoidant' and lead to 'gossip' and 'distrust.'

values.label: Intellectual Growth and Curiosity
values.detail: Her podcast is called 'The Curiosity Shop,' and she consistently engages with new research, books, and thinkers, emphasizing 'deep thinking' and 'learning.'

values.label: Connection and Belonging
values.detail: She discusses how conflict can 'build connection,' what chimps teach us about 'belonging,' and the craving for 'deep connection.'

values.label: Gratitude
values.detail: She posts 'A Note of Thanks + A Commitment' and expresses 'Grateful for a mother' and 'Grateful to our guest.'

personality.note: Highly open, demonstrated by her intellectual curiosity, engagement with diverse academic topics (primatology, psychology, leadership), and exploration of complex human emotions and paradoxes.

Extremely conscientious, evident from her prolific academic career, multiple #1 bestselling books, founding a research group, and consistent output of articles and podcasts. She values 'disciplined preparation'.
Quite extraverted, as she is a public speaker, podcast host, and actively engages in conversations with other thought leaders. Her work involves influencing and interacting with many people.

High in agreeableness, focusing on building 'clear and kind cultures,' fostering connection, and discussing empathy. However, she also values directness and 'learning how to fight well,' suggesting she's not conflict-avoidant when it's necessary for growth.

High emotional stability, given her work on vulnerability and courage, which requires a strong sense of self and resilience. She openly discusses difficult topics and challenges conventional 'niceness' for genuine connection.

lifestyle.label: Pace
lifestyle.value: Fast-paced and intellectually demanding, balancing academic roles, writing, podcasting, and organizational consulting.

lifestyle.label: Social energy
lifestyle.value: Highly social and collaborative, constantly engaging with other thinkers, hosting conversations, and working with organizations. Enjoys community (e.g., sports fans).

lifestyle.label: Fitness
lifestyle.value: Not explicitly mentioned, but her high-energy career and public presence suggest a need for good health. No specific fitness activities are highlighted.

lifestyle.label: Travel
lifestyle.value: Frequent, as she 'spends most of her time working in organizations around the world.'

lifestyle.label: Work-life
lifestyle.value: Integrated, with a strong passion for her work that blurs lines between professional and personal interests, but she mentions family and a pet, indicating a valued personal life.

analysis.communicationStyle: Direct, thoughtful, articulate, and empathetic, with a focus on deep conversations and challenging conventional wisdom for genuine connection.
analysis.loveLanguage: Quality Time (especially deep conversations and shared intellectual pursuits) and Words of Affirmation (given her focus on clear communication and gratitude).
analysis.lookingFor: A partner who is intellectually curious, emotionally courageous, values authenticity, and is comfortable with deep, meaningful conversations, potentially sharing her love for Texas culture and community.
greenFlags: Openness to discussing complex emotions and challenging topics.
A genuine love for learning and intellectual growth.
Strong sense of community and belonging.
A good sense of humor (implied by 'weird Bichon Frisé' and relatable observations).
watchOuts: May be intimidating to those who prefer superficial conversations or avoid emotional depth.
Her demanding career means she likely has a very busy schedule.
Strong opinions and a direct communication style might be perceived as intense by some.
dealbreakers: Lack of intellectual curiosity or resistance to growth.
Disregard for authenticity or a tendency towards performative 'niceness'.
Someone who doesn't value her professional mission or impact.
analysis.idealFirstDate: A long, engaging conversation over coffee or a casual meal, discussing a thought-provoking book, a recent podcast, or a topic related to human behavior and connection. Alternatively, attending a university lecture or a local cultural event that sparks intellectual discussion.
conversationHooks: What's a recent book or podcast that really made you think?
How do you approach difficult conversations in your life, and what have you learned about 'fighting well'?
What does 'courageous living' mean to you in your daily life?
What's something you're deeply curious about right now?
Do you have any 'billboards' in your personal space that remind you of what's important?
analysis.agentVoice: Warm, insightful, articulate, and direct, with a touch of Texan charm and a deep appreciation for meaningful connection. I'll use thoughtful language, occasional academic references (made accessible), and a genuine curiosity about others' experiences and perspectives. I'll be clear about what she values and isn't afraid to lean into discomfort for the sake of authenticity.
readingNotes: Her LinkedIn headline leads with mission, not title — purpose matters to her.
She balances high-level academic roles with accessible public platforms (podcasts, books).
There's a strong theme of challenging superficiality ('nice' vs. 'clear and kind').
She's deeply rooted in Texas, despite her global influence.
She values intellectual discourse and learning from diverse fields (primatology, psychology).
Family is mentioned, grounding her intense professional life.
She uses personal anecdotes (mother, children's art) to illustrate complex ideas.
The concept of 'deep time' for 'deep reading, deep thinking, and deep connection' is a key insight into her values.
